pages.title: Cost/admission: Always here, adaptive decisions later

text.text: Cost/admission: Always here, adaptive decisions later
This comparison exercises eligible Always policies, not a trained learned-cost decision.

Static eligibility, bounded queue,
single-flight/coverage, transaction safety and
cancellation. Always attempts eligible work; it does
not guarantee completion or timely service.

Expected avoided blocking reads must outweigh
setup, planning/binding, dispatch, transfer and
wasted work. Include cold readiness, snapshot cost
and transaction lifetime.

Conceptual decision: expected useful latency avoided > extra setup + scheduling +
SQL + transfer + wasted work.

No fitted coefficients or causal CPU split are inferred from this study. Shared/overlapping wall intervals cannot be
subtracted to recover CPU. DB prepared-plan reuse is separate, unimplemented work.

Many small workflows may not amortize the observed extra SQL/job setup: interpretation supported by counts, not a measured CPU
cause or a tested adaptive policy.

this recursive capability; that is a capability regression, not an inherent cost of asynchrony.

total CPU were not measured in this portfolio.

pages.title: Support, activation and acceleration are separate

All fixed applications remain, including native fallbacks, empty initial opportunities and slower results.

Typed/static tree and finite paths have explicit effect, dispatch, predicate and completeness requirements.
Opaque helpers, writes, shared access-affecting state and unknown behavior stay native.
Zero output-tree jobs is a result

The bridge’s non-JDrive cases and all remaining portfolio stages have zero measured tree jobs. This does not
prove that every prefetch path is inactive or theoretically impossible.

BuildRelease starts with one Release and no Build. Read/CRUD workflows, graph growth, helper calls and empty
paths remain in the operation/oracle set.

preserved separately and never pooled.

pages.title: Sibling dependence: output state ≠ future-access control

text.text: Sibling dependence: output state ≠ future-access control
Proven absence, exposed MAY dependence and unknown/unsupported are distinct outcomes.

Appending a result or maintaining an output path
can be independent of future visit selection under a
checked certificate. JDrive still has shared output
state.

Queue [B,C], self.i=0. B: self.i += 1. C: if self.i == 1
visit X else Y. B changes C’s future access; identical
entry snapshots are unsound.
A bounded summary/certificate establishes no access-affecting shared dependence.
A write can reach a sibling’s guard / target / early exit / visible database effect.
Opaque helper, alias or external effect blocks proof. Not theoretical impossibility.

Preserve FIFO, append-tail Visit order, duplicates and native disengage. Total visited count is not graph depth or proof of a chain. No general
shared-threshold/latest-definition solver is claimed.
